title: intelligent-serving-economics-defaults: auto-apply batching, cache, and quantization heuristics
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces intelligent defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching, and model-level quantization recommendations. Adds a new unit-economics endpoint and console UI for per-route cost suggestions. Non-breaking; opt-in via feature flag for existing customers.
body:
Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for automatic cost wins with minimal config. Teams end up copying the same batching/caching configs across routes and manually testing quantization profiles per model. This PR adds a runtime heuristic engine that proposes and can auto-apply conservative batching, prefix/KV cache settings, and quantization profiles based on workload signals and model performance profiles.

Summary of changes: 1) runtime heuristic engine (runtime/heuristics) that consumes telemetry snapshots and produces per-model/per-route suggestions; 2) batching and cache default plumbing to apply suggested configs at route creation time; 3) small quantization profile registry + selector for guarded auto-apply; 4) unit-economics reporting endpoint (/internal/cost-insights) and a Console UI panel (console/routes/cost-insights.tsx) to visualize suggested vs current unit cost; 5) migration script to seed suggestions for existing routes; 6) e2e test coverage and docs updates.

Checklist:
- [x] Heuristic engine implemented and unit tested
- [x] Safe autopilot path with feature flag redwood.cost_autopilot.enabled (default off for enterprise private)
- [x] Migration to seed existing routes (infra/migrations/2026-02-20-seed-cost-suggestions.sql)
- [x] Console UI for operators + rollout controls (canary/100% A/B)
- [x] End-to-end tests in perf-canary and redwood-quickstarts
- [x] Docs and CHANGELOG entry

Commits (high level):
- feat(heuristics): add scoring engine for batching and cache suggestions
- feat(quant): add quantization-profile registry and compatibility checks
- feat(api): new /internal/cost-insights endpoint with aggregated unit-econ data
- feat(console): cost-insights panel and per-route suggestion UI with apply/preview
- fix(runtime): guard KV cache warmup to avoid cold-start regressions
- docs: cost-optimization guide and console screenshots

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/heuristics/engine.rs (new) - scoring logic, model and route adapters
- runtime/config/defaults.rs - plumb suggested defaults into route bootstrap
- optimize/quantization/profiles.yaml - curated quant profiles with safety metadata
- api/internal/cost_insights.rs - aggregates token counts, latency, and cost model
- console/routes/cost-insights.tsx - new operator-facing UI
- infra/migrations/2026-02-20-seed-cost-suggestions.sql - seeds suggestions for existing routes
- e2e/tests/cost_profile_e2e.test.ts - end-to-end apply/rollback tests
- docs/guides/cost-optimization.md - user-facing guide and constraints

Safety notes and rollout:
- Feature flag redwood.cost_autopilot.enabled defaults to false for accounts created before rollout; it is enabled by default for new self-serve signups to demonstrate product value.
- Auto-apply behavior is conservative: only proposals with score >= 0.75 and compatibility verification (no accuracy regressions in historical evals) will be applied automatically. All auto-applies are recorded in audit logs and operator-notified via console banner.
- Quantization application is staged: we only auto-apply non-structural quantization (weight-only or symmetric int8 with runtime guardrails). Structural changes require manual approval.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for heuristic scoring and compatibility checks (added).
- Integration tests that run simulated workloads through the heuristic engine and assert expected batching/cache changes.
- E2E tests that create a temporary route, let suggestions apply, measure token-level cost delta, and rollback.
- Canary rollout on perf-canary cluster for 72 hours with A/B (10% of traffic) before full rollout.

Observability and rollback:
- Added metric redwood.heuristics.suggested_applies and redwood.heuristics.auto_applied_count.
- Console has per-suggestion confidence and rollback button.
- Automatic rollback triggers if observed latency P99 regresses >10% or accuracy regressions detected by evals.

Migration:
- infra/migrations/2026-02-20-seed-cost-suggestions.sql seeds baseline suggestions for active routes using last 7 days of telemetry. Running migration is safe and idempotent.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing route configs unchanged unless auto-apply feature flag enabled.
- No breaking API changes.

Related: ENG-4921 (cost optimization initiative), ENG-4988 (quantization rollout), SUP-324 (customer request for default cost controls).

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the quant profile compatibility checks; those are conservative and the code is intentionally explicit to ease audits.
- The heuristic thresholds are tunable via config; I included a short table in docs/guides/cost-optimization.md.
